topic.para: &snapper; is set up as an undo and recovery tool for system changes. By default, the installer formats the root partition (/) of &productname; with Btrfs and enables snapshots for it. When calculating the size of the root partition, the installer reserves additional space for snapshots.

warning.title: Enabling &snapper; after the installation changes the setup
warning.para: Enabling &snapper; in an installed system results in differences in the subvolume layout and variables, among other things. The setup then differs from the setup that this article describes.
We strongly recommend deciding whether you need snapshots before you start the installation.

topic.para: To install a standard system without snapshots, disable Btrfs snapshots for the root partition in the storage settings of the installer. In this case, you can still create snapshots manually. Keep an eye on the available disk space.

warning.title: Never disable snapshots on immutable systems
warning.para: Snapshots are essential for immutable systems. Every transactional-update run creates a new snapshot, and the system relies on these snapshots to apply changes and to roll back. Do not disable Btrfs snapshots for the root partition on these systems. For more information, see .

section.title: What does the default configuration include?
section.para: The default configuration for the root partition is stored in /etc/snapper/configs/root. Each partition or Btrfs subvolume managed by &snapper; has its own file in this directory. The file defines whether timeline snapshots are created (TIMELINE_CREATE) and the cleanup limits (for example, NUMBER_LIMIT or TIMELINE_LIMIT_HOURLY). Installation snapshots are enabled are not controlled by this file. For more information, see .
To view or change values, edit the file directly or run sudo snapper -c root get-config and sudo snapper -c root set-config "KEY=value".

Which directories are excluded is not set in this file. It is determined by the subvolume layout created at installation. For the list of excluded subvolumes, see . For detailed information about the types of snapshots and when they are created, see . For more information on the cleanup parameters, see .

section.title: Subvolumes excluded from snapshots
section.para: When &snapper; is configured to operate on root, the subvolumes listed below are excluded from snapshots by default. A rollback restores everything contained in the snapshot. If data such as user files, logs, databases or virtual machine images were part of it, a rollback would revert them to the snapshot's state, and any newer data would be lost. A rollback of the boot loader configuration could also leave the system unable to boot. Therefore, directories that hold such data are placed on separate subvolumes, which are excluded from snapshots.

listitem.para: A rollback of the boot loader configuration is not supported. The directories listed above are architecture-specific. The first two directories are present on AMD64/Intel 64 machines, the others on &aarch64;, &power; and &zseries;, respectively.
If /home does not reside on a separate partition, it is excluded to avoid the loss of user-created data on rollbacks.
These directories are used when manually installing third-party products. They are excluded to avoid uninstalling these installations on rollbacks.
The home directory of the &rootuser; user. It is excluded to avoid the loss of data on rollbacks.
Contains data for Web and FTP servers. It is excluded to avoid data loss on rollbacks.

This directory contains many variable files, including logs, temporary caches, third-party products in /var/opt, and is the default location for virtual machine images and databases. Therefore, this subvolume is created to exclude all of this variable data from snapshots and has copy-on-write disabled.

note.title: Temporary file systems
note.para: The /tmp and /run directories are not Btrfs subvolumes. They are mounted as tmpfs, which is kept in memory and not on the disk. Therefore, their content is never included in snapshots and is lost when the system reboots.
